papers.title: A Quasi-Optimal Shape Design Method for Lattice Structure Construction
papers.abstract: Lattice structures, known for their superior mechanical properties, are widely used in industries such as aerospace, automotive, and biomedical. Their advantages primarily lie in the interconnected struts at the micro-scale. The robust construction of these struts is crucial for downstream design and manufacturing applications, as it provides a detailed shape description necessary for precise simulation and fabrication. However, constructing lattice structures presents significant challenges, particularly at nodes where multiple struts intersect. The complexity of these intersections can lead to robustness issues. To address this challenge, this paper presents an optimization-based approach that simplifies the construction of lattice structures by cutting struts and connecting them to optimized node shapes. By utilizing the recent Grey Wolf optimization method -- a type of meta-heuristic method -- for node shape design, the approach ensures robust model construction and optimal shape design. Its effectiveness has been validated through a series of case studies with increasing topological and geometric complexity.

llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no mechanical testing, no stress shielding or osseointegration analysis.

summary_zh.result: 通过案例验证了方法的有效性和鲁棒性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过一系列拓扑和几何复杂度递增的案例验证。

summary_en.method: An optimization-based approach using Grey Wolf optimization for node shape design.
summary_en.result: The method ensures robust model construction and optimal shape design, validated through case studies.
summary_en.validation: Validated through a series of case studies with increasing topological and geometric complexity.

papers.title: Predictive Modeling and Uncertainty Quantification of Fatigue Life in Metal Alloys using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in machine learning-based methods have demonstrated great potential for improved property prediction in material science. However, reliable estimation of the confidence intervals for the predicted values remains a challenge, due to the inherent complexities in material modeling. This study introduces a novel approach for uncertainty quantification in fatigue life prediction of metal materials based on integrating knowledge from physics-based fatigue life models and machine learning models. The proposed approach employs physics-based input features estimated using the Basquin fatigue model to augment the experimentally collected data of fatigue life. Furthermore, a physics-informed loss function that enforces boundary constraints for the estimated fatigue life of considered materials is introduced for the neural network models. Experimental validation on datasets comprising collected data from fatigue life tests for Titanium alloys and Carbon steel alloys demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The synergy between physics-based models and data-driven models enhances the consistency in predicted values and improves uncertainty interval estimates.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文将物理模型与机器学习结合进行疲劳寿命预测并量化不确定性，其方法可迁移至生物力学植入物设计的代理建模。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on fatigue life prediction of metal alloys, not on FEA surrogate modeling for implant biomechanics or design optimization.

summary_zh.result: 在钛合金和碳钢数据集上提高了预测一致性和不确定性区间估计。
summary_zh.validation: 使用钛合金和碳钢疲劳实验数据验证。

summary_en.motivation: Machine learning-based fatigue life prediction lacks reliable uncertainty quantification due to material modeling complexities.
summary_en.method: A hybrid approach integrating physics-based Basquin model features and a physics-informed loss function into neural networks.
summary_en.result: The proposed method improves prediction consistency and uncertainty interval estimates on titanium and carbon steel fatigue datasets.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation on collected fatigue life test data for Titanium alloys and Carbon steel alloys.

papers.title: Causal Discovery via Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Existing score-based methods for directed acyclic graph (DAG) learning from observational data struggle to recover the causal graph accurately and sample-efficiently. To overcome this, in this study, we propose DrBO (DAG recovery via Bayesian Optimization)-a novel DAG learning framework leveraging Bayesian optimization (BO) to find high-scoring DAGs. We show that, by sophisticatedly choosing the promising DAGs to explore, we can find higher-scoring ones much more efficiently. To address the scalability issues of conventional BO in DAG learning, we replace Gaussian Processes commonly employed in BO with dropout neural networks, trained in a continual manner, which allows for (i) flexibly modeling the DAG scores without overfitting, (ii) incorporation of uncertainty into the estimated scores, and (iii) scaling with the number of evaluations. As a result, DrBO is computationally efficient and can find the accurate DAG in fewer trials and less time than existing state-of-the-art methods. This is demonstrated through an extensive set of empirical evaluations on many challenging settings with both synthetic and real data. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/baosws/DrBO.

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on causal graph discovery from observational data, not on surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, or biomechanical design optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有基于分数的DAG学习方法准确性和样本效率低。
summary_zh.method: 提出DrBO框架，用贝叶斯优化和dropout神经网络高效搜索高评分DAG。
summary_zh.result: 在合成和真实数据上，DrBO比现有方法用更少试验和时间找到准确DAG。
summary_zh.validation: 在多个合成和真实数据集上对比实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: Existing score-based methods for learning directed acyclic graphs from observational data suffer from low accuracy and sample efficiency.
summary_en.method: This paper proposes DrBO, a framework that uses Bayesian optimization with dropout neural networks to efficiently search for high-scoring DAGs.
summary_en.result: DrBO finds accurate DAGs in fewer trials and less time than state-of-the-art methods on both synthetic and real datasets.
summary_en.validation: Empirical evaluation on multiple challenging synthetic and real-world datasets.
